rows.title: CEO of $248 billion cybersecurity company says workers are about to face a ‘Darwinian moment’ thanks to AI: Evolve or get cut
rows.standfirst: Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora warns that 90% of employees aren’t AI savvy—and it could determine the fate of their careers.

rows.title: ‘It’s fair to ask whether it was worth it’: The Iran war has cost Americans $1,000 per household—and that’s a conservative estimate, Mark Zandi says
rows.standfirst: Gas prices, higher interest rates, and taxpayers covering military costs are adding up to quite the bill for American households.

rows.title: Today, Emily Blunt is worth $80 million thanks to her Hollywood career—but she actually wanted to be a UN Spanish translator on $80K
rows.standfirst: Emily Blunt just pocketed $15 million for “Disclosure Day,” but she once dreamed of being a translator—a job that pays $80K and is now being replaced by AI.

rows.title: Economy disappoints with half as many jobs created in June, and May and April gains revised downward
rows.standfirst: Restaurants, bars, and hotels cut 61,000 jobs, a sharp disappointment for those who expected the World Cup to boost jobs even temporarily.

rows.title: Americans are escaping the U.S. for New Zealand where house prices have hit a new low—but only wealthy Americans with $3 million spare can invest
rows.standfirst: New Zealand’s falling home prices might make it look more attainable than it has in years. But the cooling market doesn’t mean it’s suddenly open season for foreign buyers.

rows.title: ‘More fizzle than sparkle’: June jobs report fails to launch a July 4 firework
rows.standfirst: Chief economists and CIOs sounded gloomy notes. LPL Financial’s Jeffrey Roach calculated that 105.8 million Americans have left the labor market.

rows.title: Airbnb offered $750 to Americans to open up their homes during the World Cup—mostly women took it up and now they’re earning thousands
rows.standfirst: The average host short-term rental host will get a $3,000 payday for renting out their space during the World Cup. Women are jumping on the opportunity.

rows.title: On Wall Street, analysts increasingly don’t believe the U.S. government’s ‘misleading’ job numbers
rows.standfirst: “These data are misleading and should be disregarded,” Jamie Cox of Harris Financial Group says.

rows.title: Even as Elon Musk calls philanthropy ‘very hard,’ everyday Americans gave a record $617 billion—despite feeling the squeeze over the cost of living
rows.standfirst: Donations from individuals hit $394B last year, but a 17% rise in bequests points to a shift in philanthropy driven by the Great Wealth Transfer.

rows.title: A quarter of young baby boomers and Gen Xers who’ve been laid off in the last decade are still unemployed—and 11% have taken pay cuts to work
rows.standfirst: Just as financial pressure peaks, many Gen Xers are finding themselves overlooked, underpaid, and edged out.

rows.title: Costco CEO promises the $1.50 hot dog isn’t going away: ‘The price will not change as long as I’m around’
rows.standfirst: The $1.50 combo hasn’t changed since 1985. In a K-shaped economy where everything costs more, that’s not just a deal—it’s a statement.

rows.title: America’s entrepreneurial boom begins long before venture capital
rows.standfirst: Latino-owned businesses added 180,000 net new firms between 2017 and 2023 while white-owned firms declined — and the talent pipeline behind that growth runs through Minority-Serving Institutions now facing funding uncertainty.

rows.title: Billionaire Mark Cuban says it’s ‘embarrassing’ to not pay employees well—and a $20 minimum wage should be standard
rows.standfirst: Billionaire entrepreneur Mark Cuban says he’s helped mint ‘at least a thousand millionaires’, and that more employers should share success with staffers.

rows.title: Ex-PepsiCo CEO Indra Nooyi worked from midnight until 5 a.m. as a receptionist to pay for her Yale degree—and she says ‘respect went up’ because of it
rows.standfirst: The former PepsiCo CEO says grinding through overnight shifts as a Yale receptionist earned her respect no social connection could buy.

rows.title: Tech used to be a mecca for young talent—now, AI start-ups are hiring fewer entry-level talent in favor of older workers with top degrees
rows.standfirst: Tech companies like Meta built a reputation for snatching talent before they’re out of college. But now, new AI start-ups are turning away young workers.

rows.title: AI’s productivity gains are years away, but if it doesn’t deliver, it could make unsustainable debt levels even worse, Deutsche Bank economist says
rows.standfirst: Jim Reid was optimistic on AI’s ability to transform the economy, but suggested its benefits were not yet guaranteed.

rows.title: This CEO pays $1.7 million a year so employees can live in one of America’s most expensive neighborhoods
rows.standfirst: Rilla CEO Sebastian Jimenez spends around $37,000 annually on each of his 120 workers—and soon, they’ll get to enjoy an office gym and cold plunge.

rows.title: Labor force participation falls to 61.5%, the lowest in 50 years outside COVID, and economists say it’s not just people giving up
rows.standfirst: Although AI and tech innovation is blamed for that drop, it has more to do with the lack of supply relative to the number of jobs that are available.

rows.title: $5 billion CEO calls the managers that candidates didn’t list as references—and he’ll even ask coworkers they clashed with what they really think
rows.standfirst: Job seekers be warned: this CEO tracks down the managers you conveniently left off your reference list to find out what your personality is really like.

rows.title: Trump has created a ‘trickle up’ tariff economy that means U.S. companies aren’t done hiking consumer prices over import taxes
rows.standfirst: The Federal Reserve of New York found that nearly half of service firms and manufacturers anticipated raising prices as a result of tariffs.

rows.title: The housing market just split in two: Prices are falling out West and soaring in the Northeast
rows.standfirst: Home list prices have dropped 7.3% in the West since 2022 but climbed 12.6% in the Northeast, according to Realtor.com data—even as the national median sales price hit an all-time high of $440,600 in June.

rows.title: Fed’s Williams says AI is now his main inflation concern
rows.standfirst: “Monetary policy would need to respond to that,” said Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams.

rows.title: Harry Styles fans flew to Amsterdam, paid a 21% premium for hotels, and sent inflation soaring. One Gen Zer paid $1,000 for a tiny ‘box’ hotel room
rows.standfirst: Young people may be struggling with financial milestones, but Harry Styles fans in the Netherlands proved their spending power can catch bankers’ eyes.

rows.title: One Wall Street firm is paying its Gen Z interns fresh out of college $8,600 a week—more than the typical American makes in nearly two months
rows.standfirst: Susquehanna is offering master’s and Ph.D. interns up to $86,000 for a 10-week summer, plus free housing, complimentary meals, and other perks.

rows.title: More noncollege-educated men are living at home and falling out of the labor market, forcing a decline in marriages, all thanks to rising rents
rows.standfirst: “Very real economic forces” are “limiting the options for non-college-educated men,” said Gabrielle Penrose of the American Institute for Boys and Men.

rows.title: Trump undercuts GOP midterms message with snub of housing bill
rows.standfirst: As recently as June, Trump hailed the package as “the most comprehensive and consequential housing legislation in the history of our country.”

rows.title: There’s no escape from inflation as a perfect storm of the ‘Godzilla’ El Niño, AI boom, Trump tariffs, fuel crunch, and Ukraine war keep prices high
rows.standfirst: “These results suggest that many businesses are still adjusting their prices, more than a year after tariffs were first introduced.”

rows.title: Homes are in short supply in the U.S. How a new law could change the market
rows.standfirst: Its impact might not be felt for years, however, given the often long timelines on construction projects and state and local statutes that limit development.

rows.title: Brené Brown warns American workers are not neurologically wired for this level of rapid change and instability: ‘People are not okay’
rows.standfirst: “People are emotionally dysregulated, distrustful, and disconnected,” bestselling author and professor Brené Brown warned.

rows.title: Oil prices march upward again as the U.S-Iran conflict intensifies—and it’s yet another headache for Warsh and the Fed
rows.standfirst: Escalating tensions between the U.S. and Iran have knock-on effects for inflation expectations and as a result, the trajectory of the base rate, notes Goldman Sachs.

rows.title: Chipotle’s COO takes employees to dinner every week to spot his next leaders—here are the 4 traits he’s seeking
rows.standfirst: Jason Kidd, COO of the $46 billion fast-casual chain, is looking to promote talent with four key traits—team players who “own the outcome” have the best shot.

rows.title: The real reason college costs 43% of family income isn’t tuition
rows.standfirst: A 667-college database spanning 1840 to 2020 shows tuition growth actually slowed after 1990; sticker prices did not drive the affordability crisis.

rows.title: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon says he’s eyeing up book deals and teaching gigs when he steps away from his decades-long career at the banking giant
rows.standfirst: JPMorgan’s Jamie Dimon has revealed he could become a teacher after he steps down, following in the footsteps of Microsoft’s Steve Ballmer.

rows.title: Goldman economist offers a reality check on AI adoption: it took 15 years for computers to really show up in the data
rows.standfirst: Elsie Peng’s research draws an uncomfortable parallel to the PC revolution: productivity gains took 15 years to materialize last time.

rows.title: Kevin Warsh won’t say if the Fed is done raising rates, even as he says the Fed has ‘no tolerance’ for high inflation and Trump pressure looms
rows.standfirst: Warsh heads a sharply divided rate-setting committee as he spoke in his first Congress appearance to talk about the central bank.

rows.title: The first major housing law since the 1990s skips the one fix that economists say renters need
rows.standfirst: The new law streamlines environmental reviews and eases mortgage rules for cheaper homes, and leaves zoning decisions to cities and suburbs.

rows.title: He sold his last company to Palantir. Now he’s betting $32 million that robots can fix construction’s labor crisis
rows.standfirst: Monumental founder Salar al Khafaji is bringing his fleet of autonomous bricklaying robots to the U.S. this year, backed by a new Khosla Ventures-led round.

rows.title: The $21 billion company behind Eventbrite, Vimeo, and AOL has just revealed how it picked 286 out of 800,000 job applications
rows.standfirst: The $21 billion company behind Eventbrite, Vimeo, and AOL has just revealed how it picked 286 out of 800,000 job applications.

rows.title: It’s now cheaper to buy a new home than a used one, thanks to builder incentives and baby boomers who don’t want to sell on the low
rows.standfirst: There are deals to be had in the housing market right now as home builders offer incentives to move more inventory.

rows.title: Wholesale inflation falls 0.3% in June, but Iran war clouds outlook
rows.standfirst: TradeStation’s David Russell said “energy saved the day in June, but that might become ancient history if the Strait of Hormuz doesn’t open soon.”

rows.title: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon says 300,000 workers are needed to rebuild American shipbuilding—with jobs paying $100,000 without a college degree
rows.standfirst: The American Dream now runs through the skilled trades, according to Jamie Dimon—and his bank is investing $24 million to ramp up training in Philadelphia.

rows.title: U.S. companies have finally gotten $71 billion in tariff refunds, but they’re using it to offset inflation caused by the Iran war
rows.standfirst: “The Middle East conflict is really driving more inflation…so we are going to use the majority of the tariff refund to offset these higher costs,” the McCormick & Company CFO said.

rows.title: FedEx’s CEO landed his first job by taking a roommate’s abandoned interview. Now he’s running a $75 billion shipping giant
rows.standfirst: Raj Subramaniam became the second-ever CEO of FedEx by taking every opportunity thrown his way—including his roommate’s job interview.

rows.title: Goldman Sachs CEO says he’d hire someone ‘smart enough’ over the smartest person in the world because ultimately experience trumps brains
rows.standfirst: Relying on book smarts over real-life expertise won’t get one hired at the $337 billion bank, says Goldman Sachs boss David Solomon.

rows.title: Agricultural economist explains why you’re paying 32% more for lettuce and 20% more for tomatoes — and why it will stay that way
rows.standfirst: Trump’s exit from the U.S.-Mexico Tomato Suspension Agreement triggered a 17% antidumping duty, and Mexican imports have already fallen 13% year over year.

rows.title: Billionaires like Ken Griffin are moving to Miami—but middle-class earners can’t copy them and reap the same benefits, real estate experts say
rows.standfirst: Real estate experts tell Fortune those making a middle-class salary are better off renting than buying with fewer affordable homes in the Miami market.

rows.title: MIT AI expert warns automating Gen Z entry-level jobs could backfire—and cost companies their future workforce
rows.standfirst: CEOs who cut entry-level jobs risk long-term fallout, warns MIT’s Andrew McAfee—as IBM and Salesforce double down on Gen Z talent.

rows.title: The minimum wage is now the lowest it’s been in 70 years—making the federal wage floor ‘officially a poverty wage,’ report finds
rows.standfirst: “We are currently in the longest period of inaction on the federal minimum wage since its inception in 1938,” economist Sylvia Allegretto wrote in a recent report.

rows.title: Retirees wait for the day they can sell their homes and cash in—but there’s a secret Medicare ‘trap’ that could stop them in their tracks
rows.standfirst: Selling your home near retirement age can trigger a Medicare premium surcharge that costs thousands a year—and most retirees don’t find out until the bill arrives.

rows.title: Gas prices spiral over $4 as U.S.-Iran war heats up again, amid warning that ‘economic gravity’ will soon catch up to American families
rows.standfirst: “In the Wile E. Coyote scenario, economic gravity eventually exerts itself,” wrote UBS’s Paul Donovan this morning.

rows.title: Japan’s monetary conundrum — why the yen hit a 40-year low as interest rates hit a 31-year high
rows.standfirst: Japan hiked rates to chase inflation—but its real problem is money that never showed up.

rows.title: Spain’s Ferran Torres scored the winning goal in the World Cup—but just four years ago, he was in therapy and stuck in a ‘bottomless pit’
rows.standfirst: Ferran Torres said he “could not see a way out” after a $62.8 million Barcelona deal—and half of athletes struggle with mental health problems.

rows.title: $5 billion CEO says unemployed Gen Z should be out 3 days a week building their network: ‘Sometimes those jobs you want, they’re never published’
rows.standfirst: $5 billion Netskope CEO says the secret to landing a job these days isn’t just a perfect résumé—it’s showing up to enough dinners and networking events.

rows.title: Jamie Dimon says six-figure shipyard jobs are the new ‘American Dream’—but candidates will need to endure hours of extreme heat, cold, and rain
rows.standfirst: Shipyard jobs can pay upwards of $100K without a college degree—and nearly a quarter of a million maritime workers are needed. But it comes with tradeoffs.

rows.title: Mathematicians grapple with a ‘very rapid and very unsettling change’ as AI cracks yet another century-old problem
rows.standfirst: Anthropic’s Levant Alpöge, a former Harvard valedictorian, used Claude’s Fable 5 to find something that mathematicians have failed to since 1939.

rows.title: Exclusive: Stanford and ADP have new payroll data on Gen Z women losing ground to men in the job market—and AI isn’t the main culprit
rows.standfirst: Women’s employment grew just 1.3% annually since late 2022 for 22 to 25-year-olds, compared with 2.7% for men, Stanford and ADP found.

rows.title: Larry Page and Sergey Brin splash $225 million in Miami property as billionaires flee California’s tax—and Google is expanding its office there too
rows.standfirst: Larry Page and Sergey Brin now own around $225 million in Miami real estate, and other billionaires are bringing their companies to the coastal region.

rows.title: The millennial generation has split, new Fed research shows: Those over 35 are edging toward boomer-style wealth, while everyone else falls behind
rows.standfirst: A new Fed measure shows just 22% of adults under 35 actually own their home—not the 37% that the headline number suggests.

rows.title: ‘It’s called StreetEasy, not StreetHard’: Mamdani cracks down on scourge of ‘housefishing’ and ‘real estate slop’
rows.standfirst: The New York mayor’s proposal would require landlords, brokers and listing platforms to disclose AI-generated or digitally altered rental photos.

rows.title: ‘The demographic dividend of the last 40 years is ending’: J.P. Morgan says the world is running out of the two things that kept interest rates down
rows.standfirst: “The demographic dividend that characterized the last 40 years is ending,” the J.P. Morgan note reads.

rows.title: Oil at $100 is pushing up costs from gas pumps to grocery aisles
rows.standfirst: “Since everything relies on petroleum in our economy, for good or ill, if the cost of petroleum goes up, then everything else goes up as well.”

rows.title: An 11-year-old is cleaning his neighbors’ trash cans for $10 each—he now has 100K followers as teens face the worst summer job market since 1948
rows.standfirst: Ashton Meyer, 11, wanted more pocket money this summer—so he started his own bin-cleaning business, and it’s already gone viral.

rows.title: The millennial generation is split in 2: an older crowd with boomer-style comfort, a younger set going ‘back to the early 1900s’
rows.standfirst: NAR deputy chief economist Jessica Lautz sees us going back toward ”an older way of living,” but only some of us.

rows.title: ‘Rockets and feathers’: Economists say grocery prices shoot up like the first, fall like the second
rows.standfirst: “I think the public is coming to grips with, ‘Well, I’m hearing inflation has slowed, but things aren’t getting any cheaper.’”

rows.title: Meet the Americans learning to go without after the biggest grocery inflation in 50 years
rows.standfirst: “Prices are sky-high. One hundred dollars’ worth of groceries these days is nothing,” says 60-year-old Ada Torres of Cleveland, Texas.

rows.title: Let’s get ready to rumble: The next Fed meeting will be a ‘family feud’—and that’s exactly what Chairman Kevin Warsh wants
rows.standfirst: “And the survey says … policy will likely stay on hold for an additional meeting. Hawkish momentum is building, however. We expect two hawkish dissents.”

rows.title: This millennial job-hopped every 6 months to $90K by the time she was 23—she left it all behind to become a salary negotiation guru
rows.standfirst: Hannah Williams, the creator and host of Salary Transparent Street, ditched her $115,000 job to pull back the curtain on what workers really make.

rows.title: Despite nearing their 60s, nearly four in 10 Americans heading towards the end of their careers don’t even have a retirement account
rows.standfirst: Around four in 10 U.S. Gen Xers, and even some baby boomers, haven’t saved for retirement—as current retirees who didn’t save enough endure a “nightmare.”

rows.title: CEO of the top-rated hiring platform says the job market is so bad that candidates are paying $20 to mass apply and driving bosses crazy with spam
rows.standfirst: Job seekers are spamming every job with AI. Employers are using AI to filter them out. Greenhouse’s CEO says it’s created a doom loop for everyone.

rows.title: Trump can’t stop shooting himself in the foot, as the stage looks set once again for Warsh to hold—if not hike—interest rates
rows.standfirst: “After months of upside inflation surprises, patience is wearing thin,” writes EY-Parthenon’s Gregory Daco.

rows.title: Oprah Winfrey says ‘Life starts at 44’—and research proves she’s right: The average founder starts their business after 40
rows.standfirst: Billionaire Oprah Winfrey says she “locked in” in her forties—as most CEOs and founders are middle-aged.

rows.title: Why did a $154 billion CEO just endorse stripping most Americans of voting rights—and taking us back to the 19th century?
rows.standfirst: Should how much you pay in taxes determine how much your vote counts? Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke seems to think so.

rows.title: Forget your degree: Gen Z say reselling their old clothes on Depop taught them more about business than college—and 85% of hiring managers actually agree
rows.standfirst: Exclusive: Hiring managers say running a resale account impresses them more than an internship or a retail job.

rows.title: China’s exports are so huge they’re now lowering inflation in other countries
rows.standfirst: A discrepancy between China’s export data and U.S. import data is “not because ships are sinking mid-Pacific,” notes UBS’s Paul Donovan.

rows.title: Despite making over $135K, 1 in 5 high earners feel ‘depressed’ when thinking about their finances—they may have ‘money dysmorphia’
rows.standfirst: Seven in 10 Americans on six-figure salaries aren’t financially fulfilled—even wealthy Gen Zers.

rows.title: In South Korea, teenagers are skipping college for semiconductor school—they’re landing six-figure Samsung jobs at 17 and bonuses of up to $400,000
rows.standfirst: At one South Korean vocational high school, 96.4% of graduates land jobs—with many headed to Samsung and earning six-figure paychecks without degrees.

rows.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang says AI is killing tasks not jobs—and the white-collar bloodbath narrative gets the future of work ‘exactly backwards’
rows.standfirst: “AI automates tasks away, but it doesn’t necessarily eliminate jobs,” Huang said.

rows.title: A pound of ground beef now costs $6.82 — and that number is crushing consumer confidence
rows.standfirst: Inflation has climbed to 3.5% since the Iran war began, and Trump faces midterm risk as gas prices rise again.

rows.title: Foreign buyers seem to be following Zohran Mamdani’s cue — and fleeing American real estate
rows.standfirst: Foreign homebuying is near record lows, National Association of Realtors data reveals, and New York isn’t even in the top five anymore.

rows.title: Fed, in a nail-biter July meeting, decides to leave rates unchanged
rows.standfirst: The Fed’s rate-setting committee reached the 9-3 decision after two days of deliberations.

rows.title: How Washington’s war on ‘Wall Street landlords’ could backfire on Gen Z renters
rows.standfirst: John Burns Research and Consulting dubbed it the “Rental Inflation Bill,” while ResiClub’s Lance Lambert says some landlords are reluctant to get burned.

rows.title: Love Island contestants will spend their winnings on bills and loans because $100K just doesn’t go that far anymore
rows.standfirst: The average student loan won’t leave much change out of the $50,000 each individual winner will take home.

rows.title: Bank of England keeps interest rates at 3.75% for fifth time this year
rows.standfirst: The monetary policy committee voted to keep the rate, following the expectations of most economists.

rows.title: Ultra-rich are buying up $49 million mansions in London, with ‘Trump unease’ generating a 10% rise in Americans investing in Britain
rows.standfirst: In the first half of this year, Americans accounted for 30% of London’s luxury home sales above $20 million. A real estate expert blames unease over Trump.

rows.title: Nearly a third of workers admit to sabotaging their company’s AI—and smaller paychecks may explain why
rows.standfirst: As surveys document quiet resistance and outright sabotage, Apollo’s Torsten Slok offers a theory: AI is compressing wages while leaving job counts intact.

rows.title: The Fed did exactly what Wall Street was expecting—so why are markets so vexed by Kevin Warsh?
rows.standfirst: “You’re dealing with the Fed that the market is still trying to understand,” J.P. Morgan’s Alex Wolf tells Fortune.

rows.title: More than half of Gen Zers want to become influencers—so now Arizona State University is offering a content creation degree for $142K
rows.standfirst: Arizona State University is helping turn its students into influencers with a bachelor’s degree in building a social media empire.

rows.title: Kevin Warsh’s first big press conference shines a spotlight on confusion over how the Fed actually measures inflation
rows.standfirst: Is inflation 3.7% or 2.2%? It depends on which Federal Reserve number you believe.
